$comment: Starting point for <policy_dir>/claude/settings.json. It is intentionally workspace-relative so one policy can be reused for several project workspaces. chmod 600 and keep it outside every workspace. Adapt and test with the installed Claude Code version; Enso checks launch plumbing, not policy meaning.
$comment_write_boundary: Conservative read-only starting point: denying Bash/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit outright means this policy cannot write or plant files. Under --permission-mode dontAsk the Read tool defaults to allowed, so the deny list blocks only the paths it names; the sandbox block below also constrains the Read tool and does the broader read and network confinement. For a chat-only route, permissions.deny=["*"] is the simplest fail-closed shape. A policy that grants writes must also deny Write/Edit to .claude/**, .codex/**, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and skills so its workspace instructions cannot be weakened.
$comment_native_docs: Claude Code is authoritative: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference, and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills. Tool permissions do not by themselves hide native skills or slash commands; decide which native settings and scopes your installation needs, then verify them directly.
